{{etymon|en|id=furniture|:inh|enm:bed<id:furniture>|tree=1}}{{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰedʰ-|id1=bend|*bʰedʰh₂-|*bʰeh₁-}}

{{inh+|en|enm|bed}}, {{m|enm|bedde}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bedd}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*badi}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*badją|t=resting-place, plot of ground}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|bed}}, {{cog|frr|baad}}, {{m|frr|beed}}, {{m|frr|Bēr}}, {{cog|stq|Bääd}}, {{cog|fy|bêd}}, {{cog|cim|pett}}, {{cog|nl|bed}}, {{cog|nds-nl|bedde}}, {{cog|de|Bett}}, {{m|de|Bette}}, {{cog|nds-de|Bedd}}, {{cog|lb|Bett}}, {{cog|wym|bet}}, {{cog|da,nb|bed}}, {{cog|fo,is|beð}}, {{m|is|beður}}, {{cog|nn|bed}}, {{m|nn|bedd}}, {{cog|sv|bädd}}, {{cog|got|𐌱𐌰𐌳𐌹}}, all meaning “bed”.
{{col-bottom}}
{{col-top|2|further possible etymology and cognates}}
The {{inh|en|gem-pro|-}} term may in turn be from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰedʰh₂-|*bʰedʰ-|t=to dig}} with various theories explaining the development in meaning. If it is, the term is also cognate with {{cog|grc|βοθυρος||pit}}, {{cog|la|fossa||ditch}}, {{cog|lv|bedre||hole}}, {{cog|cy|bedd||grave}}, {{cog|br|bez||grave}}; and probably also {{cog|ru|бодать||to butt, gore}}.
{{col-bottom}}

# {{sid|en|Q42177}}{{lb|en|countable}} A piece of [[furniture]], usually flat and soft, on which to [[rest]] or [[sleep]].
#: {{ux|en|My cat often sleeps on my '''bed'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|I keep a glass of water next to my '''bed''' when I sleep.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Charles Johnstone|title=The Reverie; or, A Flight to the Paradise of Fools|url=http://books.google.com.sg/books?id=1mAzAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA202|volume=2|location=Dublin|publisher=Printed by Dillon Chamberlaine|year=1762|page=202|oclc=519072825|passage=At length, one night, when the company by ſome accident broke up much ſooner than ordinary, ſo that the candles were not half burnt out, ſhe was not able to reſiſt the temptation, but reſolved to have them ſome way or other. Accordingly, as ſoon as the hurry was over, and the ſervants, as ſhe thought, all gone to ſleep, ſhe ſtole out of her '''bed''', and went down ſtairs, naked to her ſhift as ſhe was, with a deſign to ſteal them{{nb...}}.}}
## {{senseid|en|mattress}} {{lb|en|countable}} A [[mattress]].
##: {{ux|en|I find her '''bed''' too soft.}}
## {{senseid|en|bedframe}} {{lb|en|countable}} A [[bedframe]].
##: {{ux|en|That huge wood '''bed''' is too heavy for us to carry it that far.}}
## {{senseid|en|prepared sleeping spot}} A prepared [[spot]] in which to spend the night.
##: {{ux|en|When camping, he usually makes a '''bed''' for the night from hay and a blanket.}}
## {{senseid|en|place of rest}} {{lb|en|usually after a preposition}} One's place of sleep or rest.
##: {{ux|en|[[go to bed|Go to '''bed''']]!}}
##: {{ux|en|I had breakfast in '''bed''' this morning.}}
## {{senseid|en|rest}} {{lb|en|uncountable|usually after a preposition}} Sleep; rest; getting to sleep.
##: {{ux|en|He's been afraid of '''bed''' since he saw the scary film.}}
## {{senseid|en|bedtime}} {{lb|en|uncountable|usually after a preposition}} The time for going to sleep or resting in bed; [[bedtime]].
##: {{ux|en|I read until '''bed'''.}}
## {{senseid|en|bed requirements}} {{lb|en|countable}} The equipment, staffing, etc., required for a patient in a medical institution.
##: {{ux|en|We have a patient who needs a '''bed''' right away.}}
## {{senseid|en|time spent sleeping}} {{lb|en|uncountable}} Time spent in a bed.
##* {{quote-book|en|author=Thomas Stretch Dowse|title=Lectures on Massage and Electricity in the Treatment of Disease|year=1903|page=276|passage=I am quite sure that too much '''bed''', if not too much sleep, is prejudicial, though a certain amount is absolutely necessary.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Jabez Spencer Balfour|title=My Prison Life|year=1907|page=181|passage=Some prisoners, indeed, are always up before the bell rings — such was my practice — they prefer to grope about in the dark to tossing about in the utter weariness of too much '''bed'''.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|author=James Verney Cable|title=Principles of Medicine: An Integrated Textbook for Nurses|year=1972|passage=This condition is one of the dangers of “too much '''bed'''”. The nurse should inspect the legs of each patient daily}}
## {{senseid|en|marriage}} {{lb|en|figurative}} [[marriage|Marriage]].
##* {{RQ:Clarendon History
|passage=George, the eldest son of his second '''bed'''.}}
## {{senseid|en|sex}} {{lb|en|figurative|uncountable}} [[sexual|Sexual]] [[activity]].
##: {{ux|en|Too much '''bed''', not enough rest.}}
## {{senseid|en|bedroom}} {{clipping of|en|bedroom}}.
##: {{co|en|2 '''beds''', 1 bath}}
# {{senseid|en|surface}} A place, or flat [[surface]] or [[layer]], on which something else [[rest]]s or is [[lay|laid]].
#: {{ux|en|The meats and cheeses lay on a '''bed''' of lettuce.}}
## {{sid|en|bottom of a body of water}}{{lb|en|countable}} The [[bottom]] of a body of water, such as an [[ocean]], [[sea]], [[lake]], or [[river]]. {{defdate|from later 16<sup>th</sup>c.}}
##: {{co|en|sea '''bed'''}}
##: {{co|en|river '''bed'''}}
##: {{ux|en|There’s a lot of trash on the '''bed''' of the river.}}
## {{senseid|en|sealife}} An area where a large number of [[oyster]]s, [[mussel]]s, other [[sessile]] [[shellfish]], or a large amount of [[seaweed]] is found.
##: {{ux|en|Oysters are farmed from their '''beds'''.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1941|author=w:Emily Carr|title=w:Klee Wyck|url=http://www.gutenberg.net.au/ebooks01/0100131h.html|chapter=18
|passage=I knew that there were [[kelp]] '''beds''' and reefs which could rip the bottoms from boats down in Skedans Bay.}}
## {{senseid|en|planted plot}} A planted [[plot]] of [[land]], a [[garden]] plot.
##: {{ux|en|We added a new bush to our rose '''bed'''.}}
##* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|chapter=Afterglow|page=168|passage=Breezes blowing from '''beds''' of iris quickened her breath with their perfume; she saw the tufted lilacs sway in the wind, and the streamers of mauve-tinted wistaria swinging, all a-glisten with golden bees; she saw a crimson cardinal winging through the foliage, and amorous tanagers flashing like scarlet flames athwart the pines.}}
## {{senseid|en|foundation}} A foundation or supporting surface formed of a [[fluid]].
##: {{ux|en|A '''bed''' of concrete makes a strong subsurface for an asphalt parking lot.}}
## {{senseid|en|railroad}} The superficial [[earthwork]], or [[ballast]], of a [[railroad]].
## {{senseid|en|platform}}{{lb|en|US|Canada|automotive}} The [[platform]] of a truck, trailer, wagon, railcar, or other vehicle that supports the [[load]] to be hauled.
##: {{syn|en|tray}}
##: {{hypo|en|truckbed}}
##: {{ux|en|The parcels were loaded onto the truck '''bed''' before transportation.}}
## {{senseid|en|timber}} A [[shape]]d piece of [[timber]] to hold a [[cask]] clear of a [[ship|ship’s]] [[floor]]; a [[pallet]].
## {{senseid|en|printing}} {{lb|en|printing|dated}} The flat part of the [[press]], on which the [[form]] is laid.
## {{senseid|en|scanner}} {{lb|en|computing}} The flat surface of a [[scanner]] on which a [[document]] is placed to be scanned.
## {{senseid|en|music}} {{lb|en|music}} A piece of [[music]], normally [[instrumental]], over which a [[radio]] [[DJ]] talks.
## {{senseid|en|darts}} {{lb|en|darts}} Any of the sections of a dartboard with a point value, [[delimit]]ed by a [[wire]].
## {{senseid|en|trampoline}} {{lb|en|trampoline}} The taut surface of a [[trampoline]].
##* {{quote-book|en|title=Sports: The Complete Visual Reference|year=2000
|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=ny_rBy0mT7wC&pg=PA68&dq=%22the+bed%22
|text=These 5 judges mark the athlete's staying in the center of the '''bed''', uniformity of bounce heights, and general style.
}}
# {{lb|en|heading}} ''A horizontal [[layer]] or [[surface]].''
## {{senseid|en|deposit}} A [[deposit]] of [[ore]], [[coal]], ''etc.''
## {{sid|en|Q806617}} {{lb|en|countable|geology}} The smallest division of a geologic formation or [[stratigraphic]] rock series marked by well-defined divisional planes ([[bedding plane]]s) separating it from layers above and below.
##: {{syn|en|layer|stratum}}
## {{senseid|en|building stone}} {{lb|en|masonry}} The horizontal surface of a building stone.
##: {{co|en|the upper and lower '''beds'''}}
## {{senseid|en|brick}} {{lb|en|masonry}} The lower surface of a brick, slate, or tile.<ref>{{R:Knight AMD}}</ref>
## {{senseid|en|wall course}} {{lb|en|masonry}} A [[course]] of stone or brick in a [[wall]].

====Usage notes====
* To prepare a bed (in the sense of sleeping furniture) is usually to {{m|en|make the bed}}, or {{qualifier|Southern US}} to {{m|en|spread the bed}}, the verb {{m|en|spread}} probably having been developed from {{m|en|bedspread}}. Like many nouns denoting places where people spend time, {{m|en||bed}} requires no article after certain prepositions: hence {{m|en||in bed|lying in a bed}}, {{m|en||go to bed|get into a bed}}, and so on. The forms {{m|en||in a bed}}, etc. do exist, but tend to imply mere presence in the bed, without it being for the purpose of sleep.

''See also [[Appendix:Collocations of do, have, make, and take]].''

===Etymology 1===
[[File:Glarus Kloentalersee.jpg|thumb|A mountain lake.]]
{{ety|en|id=body of water|:inh|enm:lake<ety:inh<ang:lacu>>|enm:lac<ety:bor<fro:lac>>|tree=1}}
Arose from a conflation of

* {{inh|en|enm|lake|t=small stream of running water, pool, lake}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lacu|t=stream, pool, pond, lake}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*laku}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*lakō|t=stream, pool, body of water", originally "a place where water runs off and collects}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leg-|t=to leak, drain}}; with
* {{noncog|enm|lac|t=lake}}, from {{noncog|fro|lac|t=lake, ditch, pit}}, a borrowed term, likely from {{noncog|la|lacus|t=lake, tub, vat}} (see {{m+|fro|lac}} for more).

The first element is related to {{cog|nl|laak|t=stream, drainage ditch, pond}}, {{cog|nds-de|Lake}}, {{m|nds-de|Laak|t=drainage, marshland}}, {{cog|de|Lache|t=puddle, pool}}, {{cog|no|løk|t=a deep, slow-moving stream; a widening in a stream or river}}, {{cog|fo|løkur|t=small brook}} and {{m|fo|lækja|t=water hole, well, watershoot in a brook}}, {{cog|is|lækur|t=stream}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|code=105167|entry=lake|pos=n.3|date=September 2021}}</ref>

Despite their similarity in form and meaning, {{m+|ang|lacu}} is not related to {{noncog|en|lay#Etymology_2|t=lake}}, {{noncog|la|lacus|t=hollow, lake, pond}}, {{noncog|gd|loch|t=lake}}, {{noncog|grc|λάκκος|t=waterhole, tank, pond, pit}}, all from {{noncog|ine-pro|*lókus|*lókus, *l̥kwés|t=lake, pool}}.<ref>{{R:gem:EDPG|head=Lagu-}}</ref>

=====Usage notes=====
* As with the names of {{m|en|[[river]]s}}, {{m|en|[[mount]]s}} and {{m|en|[[mountain]]s}}, the names of lakes are typically formed by adding the word before or after the unique term: {{m|en|Lake Titicaca}} or {{m|en|Great Slave Lake}}. Generally speaking, names formed using adjectives or attributives see {{m|en||lake}} added to the end, as with {{m|en|Reindeer Lake}}; {{m|en||lake}} is usually added before proper names, as with {{m|en|Lake Michigan}}. This derives from the earlier but now uncommon form {{m|en||lake of ~}}: for instance, the 19th-century {{m|en|Lake of Annecy}} is now usually simply {{m|en|Lake Annecy}}. There are exceptions to this generalization, however, including notably the names of the individual [[Finger Lakes]] (e.g. [[Oneida]] Lake, [[Seneca]] Lake, [[Cayuga]] Lake). It frequently occurs, however, that foreign placenames are misunderstood as proper nouns, as with the Chinese {{m|en|Taihu||Great Lake}} and {{m|en|Qinghai||Blue Sea}} being frequently rendered as {{m|en|Lake Tai}} and {{m|en|Qinghai Lake}}.

#: {{cot|en|campground#Noun|camp#Noun|encampment#Noun}}

##: {{ux|en|Hyde '''Park''' in London;  Central '''Park''' in New York}}

|passage=I roamed the streets and '''parks''', as far removed from the idea of art and pretense as I could take myself, discovering there the kind of truth I was supposed to be setting down on paper…}}
